subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: Should protected config writes performed through `openclaw config patch` inside host exec/plugin/cron contexts be blocked, provenance-tagged for explicit operator approval, or treated as already operator-approved?
rationale: The existing gateway tool guard covers model-facing `config.patch`, but the reported failure crosses a separate CLI-through-exec path and plugin cron provenance, so automation should not choose the trust boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define and enforce the protected write boundary
options.body: Remove assistant-visible config-setting hints and add a narrow guard or provenance/approval rule for protected CLI-through-exec config writes while preserving documented operator CLI usage.

options.title: Ship only error-text hardening
options.body: Treat the issue as a prompt-injection hardening bug and remove config-setting hints, leaving CLI config patch semantics unchanged for now.

options.title: Document host exec as operator-equivalent
options.body: Keep CLI-through-exec config writes trusted and document that host exec authority can mutate config, accepting the reported risk as deployment policy.

recommendation.title: Define and enforce the protected write boundary
recommendation.body: Remove assistant-visible config-setting hints and add a narrow guard or provenance/approval rule for protected CLI-through-exec config writes while preserving documented operator CLI usage.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent is the recent current-main carrier for the affected files and merged the earlier Docker diagnostic PR, making him the best routing candidate from the available history.
